words.definition: reproduction involving fusion of gametes and usually producing genetically varied offspring
words.example: Sexual reproduction combines genetic material from two gametes.

words.definition: reproduction from a single parent without fusion of gametes, usually producing genetically similar offspring
words.example: Binary fission is a form of asexual reproduction.

words.definition: a haploid reproductive cell that can fuse with another gamete during fertilization
words.example: Sperm and egg cells are gametes.

words.definition: fusion of haploid gametes to form a diploid zygote
words.example: Fertilization restores the diploid chromosome number.

words.definition: the organs and structures involved in producing, transporting and delivering male gametes
words.example: The male reproductive system produces and transports sperm.

words.definition: the organs and structures involved in producing female gametes and supporting fertilization and early development
words.example: The female reproductive system includes the ovaries and uterus.

words.definition: a male reproductive organ that produces sperm and sex hormones
words.example: Meiosis occurs in the testes during sperm production.

words.definition: a female reproductive organ that produces egg cells and hormones
words.example: Ovulation releases an egg from an ovary.

words.definition: a small motile male gamete specialized for delivering a haploid nucleus
words.example: A sperm cell uses its flagellum to move toward the egg.

words.definition: a large female gamete containing a haploid nucleus and cytoplasmic resources
words.example: An egg cell contributes most of the cytoplasm to the zygote.

words.definition: the repeating sequence of ovarian and uterine changes controlled by reproductive hormones
words.example: The menstrual cycle coordinates ovulation with preparation of the uterine lining.

words.definition: the cycle of follicle development, ovulation and corpus-luteum activity in the ovary
words.example: FSH and LH help regulate the ovarian cycle.

words.definition: cyclical changes in the uterine lining during the menstrual cycle
words.example: The uterine cycle prepares the endometrium for possible implantation.

words.definition: follicle-stimulating hormone, a pituitary hormone that promotes follicle development in the ovary
words.example: FSH stimulates growth of ovarian follicles.

words.definition: luteinizing hormone, a pituitary hormone that triggers ovulation and supports the corpus luteum
words.example: A surge in LH triggers ovulation.

words.definition: a steroid hormone involved in female reproductive development and regulation of the menstrual cycle
words.example: Rising oestrogen helps rebuild the uterine lining.

words.definition: a steroid hormone that helps maintain the uterine lining after ovulation
words.example: Progesterone levels rise after ovulation.

words.definition: release of a mature egg cell from an ovarian follicle
words.example: Ovulation normally occurs once during each menstrual cycle.

words.definition: fertilization of an egg with sperm outside the body followed by transfer of an embryo to the uterus
words.example: In vitro fertilization can assist some people with infertility.

words.definition: hormonal stimulation of the ovaries to mature and release multiple egg cells
words.example: Superovulation is often used before egg collection in IVF.

words.definition: the reproductive structure of flowering plants
words.example: A flower contains organs involved in pollination and fertilization.

words.definition: the pollen-producing part of a stamen
words.example: Pollen grains develop in the anther.

words.definition: the pollen-receptive surface of a carpel
words.example: Pollen must reach a compatible stigma for pollination to succeed.

words.definition: transfer of pollen from an anther to a stigma
words.example: Insect pollination transfers pollen between flowers.

words.definition: pollination in which pollen is transferred between different individuals of the same species
words.example: Cross-pollination can increase genetic variation among offspring.

words.definition: a genetic mechanism that prevents or reduces fertilization by a plant's own pollen or closely related pollen
words.example: Self-incompatibility promotes outcrossing in many flowering plants.

words.definition: movement of seeds away from the parent plant
words.example: Wind can contribute to seed dispersal.

words.definition: resumption of growth of a seed embryo under suitable conditions
words.example: Water uptake is required for seed germination.

words.definition: transmission of genetic information and characteristics from parents to offspring
words.example: Patterns of inheritance can be predicted using allele combinations.

words.definition: an alternative version of a gene at a particular locus
words.example: Different alleles can produce different forms of a trait.

words.definition: the allele combination or genetic constitution of an organism for one or more loci
words.example: Two individuals can have the same phenotype but different genotypes.

words.definition: the observable characteristics of an organism produced by genotype and environment
words.example: Height is a phenotype influenced by both genes and environment.

words.definition: having two identical alleles at a gene locus
words.example: An individual with two recessive alleles is homozygous recessive.

words.definition: having two different alleles at a gene locus
words.example: A heterozygous individual carries two different alleles.

words.definition: an allele that affects the phenotype when present in a heterozygote
words.example: A dominant allele is expressed in both homozygous and heterozygous genotypes.

words.definition: an allele whose effect is usually masked in a heterozygote by a dominant allele
words.example: A recessive phenotype usually requires two recessive alleles.

words.definition: the specific position of a gene or DNA sequence on a chromosome
words.example: Alleles of the same gene occupy the same locus on homologous chromosomes.

words.definition: a diagram used to predict possible offspring genotypes from parental gametes
words.example: A Punnett grid can predict genotype ratios for a monohybrid cross.

words.definition: a genetic cross investigating inheritance of one gene or characteristic
words.example: A monohybrid cross can test a simple dominant-recessive inheritance model.

words.definition: a cross between an individual of unknown genotype and a homozygous recessive individual to infer the unknown genotype
words.example: A test cross can distinguish a homozygous dominant from a heterozygous parent.

words.definition: an individual who carries a recessive allele without expressing the associated recessive phenotype
words.example: A heterozygous carrier can pass a recessive disease allele to offspring.

words.definition: a gene located on a non-sex chromosome
words.example: Many inherited traits are controlled by autosomal genes.

words.definition: a chromosome involved in sex determination and carrying sex-linked genes
words.example: Humans usually have XX or XY sex-chromosome combinations.

words.definition: the existence of more than two alternative alleles for a gene in a population
words.example: The ABO blood-group gene has multiple alleles.

words.definition: a human blood-group system determined by IA, IB and i alleles and the presence of A and B antigens
words.example: AB blood group shows codominant expression of IA and IB.

words.definition: an inheritance pattern in which both alleles in a heterozygote are fully expressed
words.example: IA and IB are codominant in the ABO blood-group system.

words.definition: an inheritance pattern in which a heterozygote has a phenotype intermediate between the two homozygotes
words.example: Incomplete dominance can produce intermediate flower colour in heterozygotes.

words.definition: the biological process by which an organism develops as one sex, often influenced by chromosomes or environment
words.example: In humans, sex determination is usually associated with X and Y chromosomes.

words.definition: inheritance of genes located on sex chromosomes
words.example: X-linked recessive traits are often more common in males.

words.definition: an inherited disorder in which blood clotting is impaired
words.example: Some forms of haemophilia are caused by X-linked recessive alleles.

words.definition: a diagram showing relationships and inheritance of a trait through generations of a family
words.example: A pedigree chart can help identify a likely mode of inheritance.

words.definition: inheritance of a characteristic influenced by many genes
words.example: Human height shows polygenic inheritance.

words.definition: variation in which phenotypes form a continuous range rather than distinct categories
words.example: Body mass is an example of continuous variation.

words.definition: a graph showing the median, quartiles and spread of numerical data
words.example: A box-and-whisker plot can compare distributions of a continuous phenotype.

words.definition: maintenance of internal conditions within ranges compatible with normal function
words.example: Homeostasis keeps blood glucose and body temperature within controlled ranges.

words.definition: the conditions surrounding cells inside an organism, including tissue fluid and blood variables
words.example: Homeostasis stabilizes the internal environment.

words.definition: a target value or range around which a regulated variable is controlled
words.example: Body temperature is regulated around a set point.

words.definition: a cell or sensory structure that detects a stimulus or change in a variable
words.example: A receptor detects deviation from a controlled condition.

words.definition: a muscle, gland or other structure that produces a response to a control signal
words.example: Sweat glands act as effectors during thermoregulation.

words.definition: a regulatory pathway in which a deviation triggers responses that reduce the deviation
words.japanese: 負のフィードバックループ
words.example: Blood-glucose regulation operates through negative feedback loops.

words.definition: the amount of glucose present in a given volume of blood
words.example: Insulin lowers elevated blood glucose concentration.

words.definition: a pancreatic hormone that lowers blood glucose by promoting glucose uptake and storage
words.example: Insulin promotes glycogen formation after a carbohydrate-rich meal.

words.definition: a pancreatic hormone that raises blood glucose, partly by stimulating glycogen breakdown
words.example: Glucagon is released when blood glucose falls.

words.definition: conversion and storage of glucose as the polysaccharide glycogen
words.example: The liver contributes to glycogen storage after meals.

words.definition: a disorder caused mainly by autoimmune destruction of pancreatic insulin-producing cells
words.example: People with type 1 diabetes require management of insufficient insulin production.

words.definition: a metabolic disorder characterized by reduced responsiveness to insulin and impaired blood-glucose regulation
words.example: Type 2 diabetes is associated with insulin resistance.

words.definition: control of body temperature within a suitable range
words.example: Mammals use behavioural and physiological mechanisms for thermoregulation.

words.definition: the temperature of tissues within an organism
words.example: Enzyme activity can be affected if body temperature changes too far from normal.

words.definition: widening of blood vessels caused by relaxation of smooth muscle in their walls
words.example: Vasodilation of skin arterioles can increase heat loss.

words.definition: narrowing of blood vessels caused by contraction of smooth muscle in their walls
words.example: Vasoconstriction near the skin can reduce heat loss.

words.definition: secretion of fluid onto the skin, where evaporation removes heat
words.example: Sweating cools the body by evaporation.

words.definition: rapid involuntary muscle contractions that increase heat production
words.example: Shivering can raise metabolic heat production in cold conditions.

words.definition: a sensory receptor in the skin that detects external temperature changes
words.example: Peripheral thermoreceptors send information about skin temperature to the nervous system.

words.definition: a thyroid hormone that influences metabolic rate and heat production
words.example: Increased thyroxin can raise metabolic activity.

words.definition: fat tissue rich in mitochondria that can generate heat, especially in infants and some mammals
words.example: Brown adipose tissue contributes to non-shivering heat production.

words.definition: mitochondrial respiration in which energy from electron transport is released mainly as heat instead of being fully captured in ATP
words.example: Brown adipose tissue uses uncoupled respiration to produce heat.

words.definition: raising of hairs by small muscles in the skin
words.example: Hair erection can trap a thicker insulating air layer in furry mammals.
